name: Firebase Realtime Database
tagline: Firebase's original JSON-tree database that syncs every change to connected clients in milliseconds.
description: Firebase Realtime Database is a cloud-hosted JSON tree that pushes changes to every subscribed client over a persistent connection. The Firebase SDKs handle offline writes and reconnection, and Security Rules control access. It predates Firestore and still wins on raw sync latency, simplicity and pricing for small, chatty payloads such as presence, typing indicators or live game state. Its limits are real, though: each database is one regional instance with caps on concurrent connections and writes, queries filter on one key at a time, and Google labels Firestore as the preferred choice for new apps. It remains fully supported and is still updated in the Firebase SDKs.

pricing.startingPrice: Spark plan: 1 GB stored, 10 GB/month downloaded, 100 connections
pricing.notes: Blaze plan bills per GB stored and downloaded; multiple database instances per project require Blaze.

scale.notes: Each instance tops out around 200k concurrent connections and ~1k writes/s; scale by sharding data across multiple instances yourself.

strengths: Lowest-latency client sync in the Firebase family
Bandwidth-and-storage billing is cheap for many small writes
Offline writes and automatic reconnection in every SDK
Very little to learn: it's a JSON tree with listeners
weaknesses: Queries can sort or filter on only one child key at a time
A single instance has hard connection and write-throughput limits
Deep JSON trees push you into denormalisation and fan-out writes
useCases: Presence, typing indicators and live cursors
notIdealFor: Large datasets with many access patterns (use Firestore)
